status_summary: Executive Order 14159 (signed 2025-01-20, published 2025-01-29 at 90 FR 8443) directs DHS in Section 11 to pursue 287(g) agreements or other means so that qualified state and local officers can perform immigration officer functions, within the law and with local consent where appropriate. Counts of agreements rose from 1,493 active agreements in 40 states as of 2026-03-02 (ICE's dashboard, as reported by Stateline on 2026-03-03) to 2,365 signed agreements as of 2026-08-21 and 2,510 as of 2026-09-15, according to news reports citing ICE's own tracker (as of 2026-09-15: 1,778 task force model, 553 warrant service officer, 179 jail enforcement model). The Secure America Act (Public Law 119-98, enacted 2026-06-10) appropriates 31,075,000,000 dollars to ICE in Section 202, available until 2029-09-30, and lists supporting coordination with state and local authorities by expanding, facilitating and implementing 287(g) agreements among its purposes, with no separate 287(g) amount; DHS announced on 2025-09-02 a program reimbursing partner agencies for trained task force officers' salary and benefits, overtime up to 25 percent and quarterly performance awards (Gov1, 2025-09-05). The Mandate's two specific asks, a memo barring denial of access without good cause and a direction that ICE take custody of all listed criminal aliens identified by partners, were not located, and the order contains neither, so the match is partial.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion, signed; Section 11 directs DHS to use 287(g) agreements or other means to let qualified state and local officers perform immigration enforcement functions, to the extent the law allows.

DHS announces a program reimbursing 287(g) partner agencies for each eligible trained task force officer's full annual salary and benefits, plus overtime up to 25 percent, with quarterly performance awards of 1,000, 750 or 500 dollars per officer tied to how well the agency helps ICE locate identified individuals; the report mentions no startup costs.
Stateline, citing ICE's online 287(g) dashboard, reports 1,493 active agreements with local police agencies across 40 states as of this date.

Public Law 119-98 (Secure America Act) enacted; Section 202 appropriates 31,075,000,000 dollars to ICE, available until 2029-09-30, and lists supporting coordination with state and local authorities by expanding, facilitating and implementing 287(g) agreements among its purposes, with no separate 287(g) amount.

CRS report on FY2026 DHS appropriations (updated this date) describes P.L. 119-98 as giving ICE about $31.1 billion, with expanding and coordinating 287(g) agreements among the listed purposes and no separate 287(g) amount.

title: Expand 287(g) partnerships with local police and bar denials of access without cause
uncertainties: ICE's 287(g) participating agencies page was opened on 2026-10-26, but the copy returned gave figures as of 2025-02-15 (60 jail enforcement model agencies in 16 states, 75 warrant service officer agencies in 11 states, 2 task force model agencies in 2 states, 39 pending applications), which suggests a cached rendering; whether the live page shows 2026 figures was not determined, and the ICE overview page gave no counts. The 2,365 and 2,510 figures therefore still come from news reports that cite ICE's tracker, and the earlier count of 1,493 active agreements as of 2026-03-02 comes from a Stateline report citing ICE's dashboard. A baseline of about 135 agreements in January 2025 and a count of 1,372 as of 2026-01-26 come from an advocacy-group analysis (FWD.us), which Stateline relays with attribution; the ICE figures as of 2025-02-15 sum to 137 agencies, consistent with that baseline, while the 2026-01-26 count remains an unverified lead at low confidence. The counts use different methods (agencies versus agreements, active versus signed), so they should not be compared closely. An ICE fact sheet and a 2020 ICE release that also opened carried older figures (42 agencies; 139 agencies in 24 states) and are not used. Executive Order 14159 was read in full on the Federal Register and contains no good-cause access rule and no custody direction tied to 287(g) partners. No DHS or ICE memo was found on good-cause denial of access, or any custody policy for aliens identified by partners; the absence is not proof that neither exists. The text of Public Law 119-98 Section 202 was read on GovInfo and ties 287(g) only to a listed purpose of the ICE appropriation. The September 2025 reimbursement program is described in a Gov1 report of 2025-09-05 and in a release of 2025-09-02 from the office of Senator Lindsey Graham on senate.gov, which states that ICE will fully reimburse participating agencies for the annual salary and benefits of each eligible trained 287(g) officer, gives an effective date of 2025-10-01 and award tiers of 1,000, 750 and 500 dollars per officer, and mentions no startup costs; the DHS release of 2025-09-02 itself did not appear in search results and was not opened. The match is partial because the program grew far beyond what the Mandate specified while its two particular asks were not found. A NewsNation report (page metadata dated 2026-06-03) citing ICE data gives 1,891 agreements as of an unstated Tuesday, consistent with the growth trend; it is not dated precisely enough for a timeline entry.
